The '''2014–15 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Louisville]] during the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], Louisville's 101st season of intercollegiate competition. The Cardinals competed in their first season in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] and were coached by [[Rick Pitino]], in his fourteenth season at U of L. The team played its home games on Denny Crum Court at the [[KFC Yum! Center]] in [[downtown Louisville]].

They finished 27–9, 12–6 in ACC play, placing 4th, and earning a double bye in the [[2015 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]]. Louisville lost its first ever ACC Tournament game to [[2014–15 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] and earned at-large bid to the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. In their 41st NCAA Tournament appearance, they defeated [[2014–15 UC Irvine Anteaters men's basketball team|UC Irvine]], [[2014–15 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team|Northern Iowa]], and [[2014–15 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] to advance to the Elite Eight where they lost to [[2014–15 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]].

On February 20, 2018, the NCAA announced that Louisville will be forced to [[Vacated judgment|vacate]] wins and records from the [[2011–12 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|2011–12]], [[2012–13 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|2012–13]], [[2013–14 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|2013–14]], and 2014–15 seasons.<ref>{{cite press release|last1=James|first1=Emily|title=Louisville men's basketball must vacate wins and pay fine|url=https://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/louisville-mens-basketball-must-vacate-wins-and-pay-fine|website=NCAA.org - The Official Site of the NCAA|accessdate=February 20, 2018|language=en|date=February 20, 2018|archive-date=February 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180220174859/http://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/louisville-mens-basketball-must-vacate-wins-and-pay-fine|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Louisville to vacate 2013 national title, take banner down after NCAA upholds penalties|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/louisville-to-vacate-2013-national-title-take-banner-down-after-ncaa-upholds-penalties/|accessdate=February 20, 2018|work=CBSSports.com|date=February 20, 2018|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Peck|first1=Jared|title=Louisville’s 2013 national basketball championship stricken from history as NCAA denies school's appeal|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-louisville/article201070839.html|work=Lexington Herald-Leader|date=February 20, 2018|language=en}}</ref>

* Akoy Agau left the team at the end of U of L's fall semester after having played only 11 minutes in three games this season. He transferred to [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]], where he will be eligible in December 2015 with two-and-a-half remaining seasons of eligibility.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12133235/akoy-agau-transferring-georgetown-hoyas-louisville-cardinals |title=Akoy Agau transfers to Georgetown |first=Jeff |last=Borzello |work=ESPN.com |date=January 7, 2015 |access-date=January 8, 2015}}</ref>
* [[Chris Jones (basketball, born 1991)|Chris Jones]] was dismissed from the team on February 22. He had been suspended from the Syracuse game on February 18 after having sent a threatening text message to a woman he had dated,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/12371006/chris-jones-formerly-louisville-cardinals-sent-threatening-text-message-woman |title=Chris Jones sent threatening text |first=Jeff |last=Goodman |work=ESPN.com |date=February 23, 2015 |access-date=February 23, 2015}}</ref> but was reinstated several days later. After playing against Miami on February 21, he missed that night's curfew, leading to his dismissal. Several days after that, Jones was charged with rape stemming from an incident that allegedly occurred the night of the Miami game.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/forde-minutes-035848950-ncaab.html |title=Forde Minutes: College basketball narrative takes dark turn as March arrives |first=Pat |last=Forde |authorlink=Pat Forde |publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |date=March 3, 2015 |accessdate=March 10, 2015}}</ref> In late April, a grand jury chose not to indict Jones and his two co-defendants in the case.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.wdrb.com/story/28931246/grand-jury-decides-not-to-indict-chris-jones-and-co-defendants-in-rape-case2 |title=Grand jury decides not to indict Chris Jones and co-defendants in rape case |first=Jason |last=Riley |publisher=[[WDRB]] |location=Louisville, KY |date=April 29, 2015 |accessdate=April 29, 2015}}</ref>
